test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (JSO) 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: If α is the level of significance and if (1 - α) is increased, then the width of the confidence interval of mean:
solution:
The correct answer is **increases.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Increasing (1 - α) increases the width of the confidence interval of the mean:**

 
 
• The confidence interval represents the range within which the true population parameter is expected to lie, given a certain level of confidence (1 - α).
 
• When (1 - α) increases, it means we are increasing our confidence level, for example, from 95% to 99%.
 
• To accommodate this higher confidence level, the confidence interval must widen to ensure that the true population parameter is captured within this interval more often.
 
• In a financial enterprise, this means we can be more certain about the average values of financial metrics but at the cost of a broader range, which might affect precision in decision-making.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Remains constant:**

 
 
• This is incorrect. The width of the confidence interval does not remain constant when (1 - α) changes. It adjusts to reflect the new confidence level.
 
 
 
• **Is reduced by half:**
 
 
• Incorrect. The width of the confidence interval cannot be reduced by half simply by changing the confidence level. It actually increases as the confidence level increases.
 
 
 
• **Decreases:**
 
 
• Incorrect. Increasing (1 - α) or the confidence level results in an increased, not decreased, confidence interval width to ensure a higher probability of capturing the true mean.
